public_rationale: Stack Overflow reports that 51% of professional developers used AI daily. JetBrains independently finds majority adoption in fieldwork ending in June 2025. Together these satisfy the ordinary majority reading within months of publication. They do not establish universal adoption, which the wording does not require.
limitations: These are self-reported surveys, not a census.
Professional developers are a proxy for trained coders.
Survey weighting cannot eliminate every selection bias.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most or all trained coders will soon use AI as part of their workflow, if they are not already.

statement.excerpt: To be sure, most or all trained coders will (if they are not already) soon use AI as a part of their workflow.

from_speaker: use AI as a part of their workflow
our_interpretation: Most means more than half; the wording does not require universal adoption.
Professional developers are a practical proxy for trained coders.
Count actual use in software development, including occasional assistance. Plans to adopt do not count.
Soon supplies no fixed deadline. Majority adoption measured within several months of publication can establish success without inventing a terminal deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Credible broad developer surveys establish actual AI use by a majority of professional developers at publication or shortly afterward.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A survey below 50% would oppose current majority adoption but would not conclusively falsify this forecast without a deadline.

evidence.excerpt: 51% of professional developers use AI tools daily.

evidence.explanation: Daily use alone exceeds half of professional respondents. This avoids counting respondents who only plan to adopt AI.

evidence.locator: AI proficiency is becoming a core skill
evidence.explanation: The complementary adoption share is 85%, corroborating majority use. June identifies the end of the April–June survey fieldwork, not a single adoption date.
The fieldwork occurred within roughly three months after Marcus's post. The methodology describes weighting and acknowledges possible remaining selection bias.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The April–June survey records actual majority adoption shortly after publication, corroborated by professional-developer usage in e1.
